title: Rory and the Moonlit Lagoon
verses:
The stars started blinking above in the deep,
As Rory walked slowly along through the glade.
The sleepy old forest was falling asleep,
While shadows were stretching across every shade.

High up in the branches, Nia pointed the way,
To where a warm puddle was bubbling with steam.
They walked through the ferns at the end of the day,
To rest in the glow of a silver moonbeam.

Then Psittaco snuggled in moss on the ground,
While Ricky stopped running to rest by the tree.
A magical quiet was spreading around,
As peaceful and gentle as night-time could be.

Then Benny walked over to shield from the chill,
And Tilly curled up in a circle of stone.
The night grew so quiet and calm on the hill,
Where nobody ever felt lost or alone.

Now Rory closed eyes that were sleepy and slow,
And rested his head on a cushion of green.
The sky was lit up with a velvety glow,
The sweetest night landscape that ever was seen.

The moonlight was kissing the sleepy lagoon,
While all of the dinos were dreaming at last.
Beneath the soft light of a shimmering moon,
As all of the worries of daytime had passed.

title: Rory and the Moon-Blossom Meadow
verses:
The moon floated high over valleys of green,
As Nia flew down through the cool evening air.
The softest moon-blossoms that ever were seen
Were blooming in silver to shelter them there.

Then Ricky bounced over the moss with a leap,
While Psittaco nestled right into a bloom.
The valley was turning so quiet and deep,
As starlight chased away darkness and gloom.

Now Benny leaned down at the calm river side,
To block the cool breezes that blew from the steep.
And Tilly spread petals and fern leaves out wide,
To welcome her friends to a cozy deep sleep.

Then Rory stepped down where the silver weeds glow,
And curled up to rest in a soft mossy nest.
He yawned as he watched the moon flicker so low,
Content that his friends were all feeling their best.

Psittaco rested a slumbering head,
While Ricky lay still in the pale starry light.
With moss for a blanket and leaves for a bed,
They snuggled together to sleep in the night.

The river ran softly in shadows so deep,
As darkness reached over the hills from afar.
And Rory closed eyes as he drifted to sleep,
Safe under the glow of the very first star.

title: Rory and the Starlight Cavern
verses:
When evening descended on moss-covered trees,
Then Rory walked slow through the shadowy lane.
Nia swooped down on a whispering breeze,
To guide all her friends from the incoming rain.

Psittaco rested on blankets of leaves,
While Ricky crept over to curl on the floor.
The night-wind blew softly beneath the high eaves,
As Benny let out a grand slumberous snore.

They marched to a canyon where starlight shone clear,
And Tilly stepped first in the glowing blue stream.
The waters ran softly and cool for the year,
To carry each friend to a sleepy young dream.

High up in a cavern of silver and stone,
Where fireflies danced in a circle of light,
Rory sat down with a warmth of his own,
And watched as the valleys turned quiet and white.

Benny lay heavy and still on the moss,
While Nia tucked under a canopy wide.
They counted the sleepy stars drifting across,
With Ricky and Tilly tucked safe at their side.

The shadows grew long as the night settled down,
And Psittaco yawned in a sleepy embrace.
Now Rory closed eyes over forest and town,
As peace settled over this magical place.

title: The Secret of the Whispering Falls
verses:
The sun dipped away behind ridges of blue,
When Nia swooped low with a chirp of delight.
She led all her friends through the shimmering dew,
To find where the waterfall glowed in the night.

Behind the cool spray was a wide, hidden shelf,
Where giant soft ferns caught the mist in the air.
Each dinosaur found a dry spot for itself,
Content with the magical calm waiting there.

Psittaco gathered dry leaves in a heap,
And made a small cushion right next to the wall.
His chirps turned to whispers, preparing for sleep,
Entranced by the soothing cascade of the fall.

Then Ricky and Benny worked side by side now,
To roll a large boulder to block out the chill.
With teamwork complete and a yawn from the brow,
They felt all the bustle of daytime go still.

Sweet Tilly leaned close to the thunder-soft sound,
Her heavy tail resting along the damp stone.
A blanket of tranquility settled around,
Ensuring that nobody rested alone.

Green Rory sank down with a satisfied sigh,
His mighty green tail curled up close to his chest.
With moon-shadows drifting across the dark sky,
The friends closed their eyes and surrendered to rest.
